system_description.narrative_title: Escalation and internationalisation of the Russia–Ukraine war
system_description.narrative_summary: A concentrated wave of intensified Russian strikes on Ukrainian cities and infrastructure, and reciprocal Ukrainian strikes and novel weapons use, is driving rapid escalation and wider international involvement. NATO and European states are reshuffling forces, debating aid and sanctions, and confronting spillovers — from arms-technology links with North Korea to Russian influence in the Sahel — producing political strain, market disruptions and the risk of broader confrontation.
system_description.scope: Kinetic and non-kinetic interactions tied directly to the Russia–Ukraine conflict during the news window: Russian strikes and declared doctrines; Ukrainian counterstrikes and weapons innovation; NATO/European military deployments and force postures; sanctions, diplomatic moves and funding disputes; third‑party state and proxy alignments (e.g., North Korea, Belarus, Sahel juntas); near-term security incidents and commercial impacts (shipping, energy, trade, critical minerals).
system_description.super_system: The global geopolitical order / great-power competition (security, economic and diplomatic architecture linking Russia, the West, China and regional actors).
adjacent_subsystems: European security and NATO deterrence posture
Global energy, shipping and commodity markets
Arms proliferation and proxy alliances (North Korea, Sahel, Iran)
EU politics, sanctions regime and funding mechanisms

variables.name: Kinetic strike intensity
variables.description: The rate and geographic concentration of direct kinetic attacks on military and civilian infrastructure over time.

variables.name: Weapons innovation rate
variables.description: The speed at which new weapon types, delivery systems, or tactical doctrines are developed, tested and fielded.

variables.name: Military force posture
variables.description: The aggregate level of deployed forces, readiness, and forward positioning across the theatre.

variables.name: Alliance cohesion
variables.description: The degree of policy coordination, mutual support and synchronized action among aligned actors.

variables.name: Sanctions pressure level
variables.description: The cumulative intensity and coverage of economic and financial coercive measures applied to target economies.

variables.name: Arms and technology proliferation
variables.description: The flow rate of military hardware, dual‑use technologies and technical know‑how crossing between actors and proxies.

variables.name: Proxy alignment level
variables.description: The extent and stability of third‑party proxy alignments, support networks and proxy force activation.

variables.name: Supply chain disruption
variables.description: The degree to which critical commodity, transport and industrial supply chains are interrupted or constrained.

variables.name: Escalation risk perception
variables.description: The perceived probability that ongoing actions will trigger broader, higher‑intensity or interstate escalation.

variables.name: Hybrid operations intensity
variables.description: The frequency and scale of non‑kinetic hostile actions such as cyberattacks, disinformation campaigns and legal/administrative coercion.

variables.name: Defense industrial capacity
variables.description: The available production, repair and sustainment capacity for military equipment and munitions.

variables.name: Market volatility linked to conflict
variables.description: The amplitude and persistence of financial and commodity market fluctuations attributable to conflict dynamics.

variables.name: Diplomatic engagement level
variables.description: The intensity and frequency of formal and informal diplomatic negotiations, mediations and high‑level contacts.

variables.name: Public war fatigue
variables.description: The prevailing level of public support, tolerance or opposition in key populations for continued conflict and costly support measures.

variables.name: Legal norms strength
variables.description: The robustness and enforceability of international legal and normative constraints on the use of force and wartime conduct.

variables.name: Logistics and resupply capacity
variables.description: The ability to sustain operational forces through transport, stockpiles and distribution of fuel, ammunition and materiel.

catalysts.title: Alleged Russian 'massive attack' preparations
catalysts.description: Intelligence warnings and Russian rhetoric indicate a likely near-term intensification of strikes and large-scale offensive action against Ukraine.
catalysts.rationale: Zelenskiy: intelligence shows Russia is preparing massive attack; Russia pledges to continue massive strikes on Kyiv.

catalysts.title: EU envoys set to approve major Russia sanctions
catalysts.description: Scheduled EU envoy meeting expected to approve a package of new sanctions targeting Russia, increasing economic pressure and coordination.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'EU envoys set to approve major new Russia sanctions on Wednesday.'

catalysts.title: North Korea missile drills and reported Russia tech links
catalysts.description: North Korea's missile/hypersonic drills plus Ukrainian claims of shared jet-drone tech indicate accelerating transfer and testing of advanced capabilities.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'North Korea ... intermediate-range strategic missile drill'; 'Ukraine believes Russia shared jet-drone technology with North Korea.'

catalysts.title: U.S. recalls B-1 bombers from UK bases
catalysts.description: Removal/recall of B-1 bombers from UK airbase following alleged terror/drone threats alters U.S. forward posture and NATO force distribution.
catalysts.rationale: Multiple headlines: 'US removes B-1 bombers from UK base amid security concerns'; 'US recalls B-1 bombers from UK air base.'

catalysts.title: Sweden to deploy Patriot missiles to Poland
catalysts.description: Planned deployment of Swedish Patriot batteries to a NATO hub in Poland increases air-defense coverage and deterrence in the eastern flank.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Sweden to deploy Patriot missiles to NATO hub in Poland.'

catalysts.title: Ukraine deploys FP-7 ballistic and robot offensive
catalysts.description: Ukraine's first combat use of FP-7 tactical ballistic missile and intensified robotic/drone offensives indicate deeper strike capability and doctrinal shifts.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Ukraine deploys FP-7 tactical ballistic missile in combat'; 'Ukraine’s surprise robot offensive...'

catalysts.title: U.S. sends third carrier and troops to Middle East
catalysts.description: U.S. redeployment of carrier strike group and thousands of troops to the Middle East shifts strategic focus and resources away from Europe.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'U.S. Sending Third Aircraft Carrier, Up to 10,000 More Troops, to Middle East.'

catalysts.title: Baltic posture shifts and nuclear-arms debate
catalysts.description: Estonia's troop repositioning and neighbor moves to lift nuclear bans are driving Baltic/Polish defence posture changes and Russian warnings.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Estonia shifts troops closer to Russia'; 'Lithuania ... push to lift ban on nuclear weapons; Kremlin warns.'

catalysts.title: Hungary set to drop veto on EU progress for Ukraine/Moldova
catalysts.description: An expected Hungarian move to lift its veto unlocks EU political momentum and potential coordinated measures for Ukraine and Moldova.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Hungary set to drop veto on Ukraine and Moldova EU bid progress.'
